pages.title: What Easel is
pages.summary: One company's next twelve months of revenue, costs, hiring and cash, with the arithmetic behind every number.

pages.title: Run Easel
pages.summary: Get Easel and start it on your own computer with one line, signed in as the owner.

pages.title: Set up your plan
pages.summary: Name the company, choose the fiscal year, then add departments, planning lines and people.

pages.title: Build the plan
pages.summary: Revenue drivers, positions, expenses, shared costs and opening cash, and how to read any number's arithmetic.

pages.title: Run the budget cycle
pages.summary: Request department submissions, return or approve them, and freeze the budget exactly as approved.

pages.title: Scenarios and proposals
pages.summary: Branch a downside, compare profit and closing cash month by month, and promote proposals at an exact revision.

pages.title: Close the month
pages.summary: Replace a month with actuals, explain each variance, and publish the review pack.

pages.title: Move in your actuals and spreadsheet
pages.summary: Bring in a general-ledger CSV and an Excel planning workbook, preview them, accept them, and undo them.

pages.title: Back up and restore
pages.summary: Export the whole installation to one file and restore it on another computer.

pages.title: People and access
pages.summary: Who can see and change what: finance, contributors and viewers, and private pay.

pages.title: Share it with your team
pages.summary: Check a deployment locally, then put Easel on your own account for the people who plan with you.
